spaccanapoli: Spaccanapoli is the straight street that splits the old centre in two, between palazzi, churches and washing lines. A side street, Via San Gregorio Armeno, is the street of nativity scenes: the workshops sell figurines of shepherds, saints and famous people, to give as gifts or just to look at.
sansevero: Sansevero Chapel and the Veiled Christ

A small 18th-century chapel with a masterpiece: the Veiled Christ, a marble statue with a veil so fine it looks like real cloth. Around it are other sculptures and, below, the two "anatomical machines".
santachiara: Santa Chiara and the majolica cloister
A large Gothic basilica with a hidden cloister: a garden with 72 pillars and benches covered in majolica tiles painted with country scenes and Neapolitan life. It's the quietest spot in the centre.
piomonte: Pio Monte della Misericordia and Caravaggio

In a small octagonal church hangs "The Seven Works of Mercy", the large painting Caravaggio made in Naples in 1607, showing good deeds as street scenes. The gallery upstairs has more 17th-century paintings.
duomo: Cathedral and the Chapel of San Gennaro

The cathedral dedicated to Naples' patron saint, San Gennaro. In the Treasury Chapel, with its frescoes and silverwork, is kept the phial of his blood, which liquefies three times a year in front of the faithful. On one side is the older basilica of Santa Restituta, with a museum.
mann: One of the world's most important archaeological museums. It holds the mosaics, frescoes and objects from Pompeii and Herculaneum, the Alexander Mosaic, the colossal statues of the Farnese collection, such as the Farnese Hercules and Bull, and the "Secret Cabinet" of ancient erotic art.
plebiscito: Piazza del Plebiscito and Galleria Umberto I

Naples' largest square, enclosed by a semicircular colonnade with the church of San Francesco di Paola, opposite the Royal Palace. A little further on are the Teatro San Carlo, one of Europe's oldest opera houses, and the Galleria Umberto I, an elegant arcade with an iron-and-glass dome.
reale: The Bourbon residence, with its grand staircase, historic apartments with furniture and tapestries, the court theatre and the Royal Chapel. From the windows you see the bay and Vesuvius. The Romantic Garden next door is free.
castelnuovo: The medieval castle with five round towers overlooking the port, built in the 13th century by the Angevins. Inside are Alfonso of Aragon's marble triumphal arch, the Hall of the Barons and the Palatine Chapel with remains of frescoes.
ovo: Naples' oldest fortress, on an islet linked to the mainland by a causeway. From the terraces you see the bay, Vesuvius and the city. Around it is Borgo Marinari, a fishing village with restaurants on the little harbour.
sanmartino: Certosa di San Martino and the Vomero

A former monastery on the Vomero hill, with its great cloister, gardens and a museum of nativity scenes, carriages and paintings. From the terraces you see all of Naples, the bay and Vesuvius: one of the city's finest views.
sotterranea: A guided tour beneath the old centre: you go down 40 metres among the cisterns of the Greek and Roman aqueduct, tunnels and a Roman theatre, and see the shelters Neapolitans used during the bombing of the Second World War.
quartieri: Spanish Quarter and the Maradona mural
A grid of narrow, steep lanes full of everyday life: washing lines, street shrines, workshops and scooters. The Maradona mural in the lanes has become a place of pilgrimage for fans.
